name: Clemenceau Bridge
facts: Clemenceau Bridge, named after French Prime Minister Georges Clemenceau who visited Singapore in 1920, first opened in 1940 and stretched 100 metres long and 18 metres wide.
Boats can pass beneath Clemenceau Bridge up to 2 metres high, a clearance that made it a vital waterway link for Singapore’s bustling river traffic.
After demolition in 1989 to accommodate the Central Expressway, the bridge was rebuilt in 1991, with its ITS Centre completed in 2000, marking a modern engineering milestone.
